references.text: The parallel commandment in the Ten Commandments in Exodus 20, where the same prohibition against adultery is given at Sinai.
The penalty for adultery is set forth here, showing the seriousness of the commandment in Deuteronomy 5:18.
Proverbs warns that whoever commits adultery lacks sense and destroys themselves.
God calls Israel to turn back from adultery, used as a picture of spiritual unfaithfulness.
Jesus quotes this commandment and expands it to include lust in the heart, not just the physical act.
Jesus mentions this commandment as part of the commands one must keep to have eternal life.
Jesus quotes the commandment against adultery in his conversation with the rich young man.
Luke's version of Jesus' quotation of the commandment against adultery.
Paul quotes this commandment as part of the law that is fulfilled through love.
James refers to the commandment against adultery to show that the law is a unity, and breaking one commandment is to break the whole law.
